what_this_is: How the cost of a degree-41 discrete logarithm moves with the size of a subgroup factor base, and the rule that follows for choosing one: a sweep of base sizes measuring the decomposition rate and the cost of a trial, then two end-to-end runs over 256 targets at the two sizes that matter.
the_model: With a subgroup base the decomposition rate is the |F|^3/(3! r) a random base gives, and an m = 3 trial costs |F| table lookups, so work per target falls as r/|F|^2 — four times cheaper per doubling — until the rate saturates at one witness per trial and further growth only makes each trial dearer. The pair table is quadratic in |F|, so the precompute rises four times per doubling at once.
how_to_choose: Base size is a function of how many targets share the database. Total cost is precompute(|F|) + T * descent(|F|). Measured: 3.0 s + T*16.2 ms at 5248 points against 9.0 s + T*7.2 ms at 10496, so the larger base wins beyond about 665 targets and loses below it. Both beat the rho baseline's 121 ms/target above roughly 29 and 85 targets respectively.
what_this_is_not: Not asymptotic: this chooses a constant; work per target is still Theta(r/|F|^2).
Not a single-instance result: every whole-process figure amortises one precompute over many targets.
Not independent: one build, one host, one series per configuration.
Applies to the pair-table oracle only; the algebraic oracles need a linear base.
